title: Playing in Eddie Barefield's big band, 1936-37
summary: Howard says he played with Barefield in 1936-37 but tired of his hard playing.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Let's see, if there's anybody else who's--
Eddie Barefield (phonetic). Now do you know that man?
He was playin' with us, too.
Where did you meet him, Los Angeles or in San Francisco? Where, where'd you meet him Eddie Barefield and when?
Do You have an idea about what year it was?
No, I don't. I have no idea. It may come to me sometime; if it do, I'll call you up and tell you.
It says here that "Paul Howard played in Eddie Barefield's big band in 1936 and '37." Is that right?
So you'd met him before, you had? Okay.
So you'd probably met him before that, naturally. Did you enjoy him as a man and as a musician?
Oh, yeah, he was very much a man.
But I got tired of him 'cause he was wearin' me out. (laugh)
Wearin' you out, in what way?
Oh, you know, he had to play hard.
Yeah, he was a hard player. Yeah.
I hear he's doin' quite well in the East, know, still playing and everything.
No, well, he's in New York now.
Well, he played in San Francisco a long time.
So you enjoyed working with him, though?
